title: Did Pirates Actually Bury Treasure?
hook: Almost no pirate ever buried chests of Spanish gold.

scenes.text: Treasure Island and pirate legends convinced the world that buccaneers constantly buried iron chests on remote tropical islands.
scenes.imagePrompt: Weathered antique treasure map with burned edges, red 'X' mark, and sea monster illustrations on parchment. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: Treasure Island and pirate legends convinced the world that buccaneers constantly buried iron chests on remote tropical islands.

scenes.text: In reality, in the entire Golden Age of Piracy, only one famous pirate ever confirmed burying loot: Captain William Kidd.
scenes.imagePrompt: Gloomy sandy shoreline on Gardiners Island, New York, with dunes and autumn coastal grasses under stormy skies. 2D flat cartoon illustration, thick dark outlines, warm muted palette, hand-painted textures, vertical 9:16, no people in the foreground, no text, no logos
scenes.voicedText: In reality, in the entire Golden Age of Piracy, only one famous pirate ever confirmed burying loot: Captain William Kidd.

scenes.text: Kidd buried his gold near New York purely as a desperate bargaining chip to avoid being hanged by British authorities.

scenes.voicedText: Kidd buried his gold near New York purely as a desperate bargaining chip to avoid being hanged by British authorities.

scenes.text: Real pirate plunder wasn't just gold: it was silk bolts, barrels of flour, tobacco bales, nails, and precious gunpowder.

scenes.voicedText: Real pirate plunder wasn't just gold: it was silk bolts, barrels of flour, tobacco bales, nails, and precious gunpowder.

scenes.text: Pirates had notoriously short life expectancies and divided their silver immediately to spend every penny in taverns in Port Royal and Nassau.
